package_info.package_name: Konni RAT Campaign (malicious document and payloads)
package_info.why_malicious: The package chain is designed to covertly deliver and execute a remote access trojan (RAT) on Windows systems, leveraging document macros, batch scripts, DLLs, and UAC bypass to gain persistence, exfiltrate data, and provide remote control to attackers.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: VBA script retrieves OLEFormat.IconLabel, writes to temp.zip, extracts, and runs check.bat with vbHide.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On document open (with macro enabled), the code extracts an embedded payload from the document, writes it to disk, and silently executes a batch script to begin the infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros extracting and executing files are a classic initial access vector for malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate documents should not execute hidden scripts or drop executables.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted environments (rare).
key_indicators: Extraction and execution of embedded payload

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Batch script checks for remote session, OS version, architecture; renames DLLs; executes wpns.dll with parameters for UAC bypass.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After macro execution, the script prepares the environment, selects UAC bypass method, renames payloads, and launches the UAC bypass DLL with elevated privileges.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Batch scripts that manipulate DLLs and invoke UAC bypass are highly indicative of malware staging.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal batch scripts do not perform privilege escalation or DLL manipulation.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: DLL launches wusa.exe, duplicates its token, and uses CreateProcessWithLogonW to run netpp.bat with elevated privileges.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During privilege escalation, the code abuses a trusted Windows binary to bypass UAC and launch the next stage with SYSTEM-level privileges.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abuse of wusa.exe and token duplication for privilege escalation is a known malware technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs do not perform UAC bypass or launch scripts with stolen tokens.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Batch script stops netpp service, copies payloads to System32, creates/starts service 'netpp', adds registry keys for persistence, deletes traces.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After privilege escalation, the script installs the RAT as a Windows service, configures persistence via registry, and cleans up evidence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Installing unauthorized services and manipulating registry for persistence is a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers do not create covert services or erase installation traces.

execution_context.trigger: service start (system boot or manual start)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: DLL loads API functions, decrypts C2 config from netpp.ini using AES-CTR, collects system info (systeminfo, tasklist), compresses and encrypts data, uploads to C2 via HTTP POST, fetches/executes C2 commands.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On service start, the code establishes C2 communication, exfiltrates system data, receives and executes remote commands, and removes evidence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated data exfiltration, encrypted C2, and remote command execution are core RAT behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate services do not communicate with external C2s or execute arbitrary commands.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Handles C2 commands: executes commands, downloads files, uploads files, processes base64/AES-encrypted payloads.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon receiving C2 instructions, the code can execute arbitrary commands, transfer files, and process encrypted payloads, enabling full remote control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Arbitrary command execution and file transfer on attacker instruction is the essence of RAT malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate service should accept and execute arbitrary remote commands.

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious Word document and enables macros, triggering payload extraction and execution.
Batch script prepares environment, selects UAC bypass, and launches DLL for privilege escalation.
DLL abuses wusa.exe to bypass UAC and launches next batch script with elevated privileges.
Batch script installs RAT as a Windows service, configures registry persistence, and cleans up traces.
RAT DLL loads, decrypts C2 config, collects and exfiltrates system data, and establishes C2 communication.
RAT receives and executes attacker commands, enabling full remote control and further data exfiltration.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing attacker control and data theft

behavioral_signatures: Document macro extracting and executing hidden batch scripts
Batch scripts renaming DLLs and launching UAC bypass modules
DLLs abusing wusa.exe and CreateProcessWithLogonW for privilege escalation
Creation of new Windows services with uncommon names (e.g., 'netpp')
System information and process list exfiltration
network_indicators: HTTP POST to up.php with parameter name=%PCNAME%
HTTP GET/POST to dn.php with parameters name=%PCNAME% and prefix
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents spawning hidden processes (e.g., cmd.exe, batch scripts), creation of suspicious services (e.g., 'netpp'), registry modifications for persistence, and outbound HTTP traffic to known C2 domains or to up.php/dn.php endpoints. Look for AES-encrypted configuration files (netpp.ini) and unusual use of wusa.exe for privilege escalation. Correlate temporary file creation and deletion with network exfiltration events.
